answer: Give every agent a small garden plot it must tend before it can trade: a kernel of reputation earned only by keeping the plot productive across many epochs, with harvests checked by unrelated neighbours. A hollow identity that buys its way in still has to water, weed and wait, because the plot yields nothing until a full season of verified work has passed. Sybil farms face a hard limit: each fake agent needs its own plot, its own season and its own neighbours' checks, so mass-producing identities costs more land, time and attention than honest work returns.
